assertions.notes: It says German and Finnish words grow most in short strings like column headers and footer actions, and says to budget for short strings to double or triple.
It recomputes column widths from lipgloss.Width of the translated header and widest value on locale load and resize, instead of using the English header width.
It recommends a lengthened pseudo-locale with markers and a full-width pseudo-locale, and says to test with them before translations arrive.

It gives a 60–79 width band (status becomes a symbol, short headers, MM-DD dates), drops a column below 60, truncates cells with … and moves full values to a detail view, keeps ? help visible while dropping lower-priority hints, and shows a German example at 60 columns.
It says to use lipgloss.Width instead of len(), notes that 絞り込み is 4 characters but 8 cells, and gives translators budgets in cells.
States German/Finnish are long and that short strings grow the most (100–200% for <10 chars), naming column headers and footer hints.
Says to stop sizing from English and compute column widths at runtime from the wider of the translated header and data.
Recommends a pseudo-locale with ~50% longer, marker-wrapped strings plus a fullwidth variant, tested before translations arrive.
Defines 60–79 and sub-60 bands: drop Owner to a detail view, truncate Title with an ellipsis, cut headers with full text in ? help, and keep ? help visible in the footer.
Explains that 期限 is 2 characters but 4 cells, that len()/rune counts misalign, and to use lipgloss.Width().
States translations grow most on short strings, allowing 100–200% for strings under 10 characters, and names headers, statuses and key hints.
Computes column widths in WindowSizeMsg from lipgloss.Width of the current locale's header and widest value, and says to stop sizing from English.
Recommends a pseudo-locale with strings about 50% longer, wrapped in markers, plus a fullwidth CJK variant, all before translations exist.

Shows a German mockup at 60 columns where Priority moves to the detail view, titles truncate with an ellipsis, footer hints drop from the end with ? help kept early, and a too-small message names the real minimum.
Says to measure in cells, gives 優先度 as 6 cells not 3, warns against len() and fmt rune padding, and covers ambiguous-width characters.

Recommends a plain normal-mode key like `b` or a leader sequence, avoiding Ctrl+B and screen's Ctrl+A, with a keymap test enforcing this.
Suggests checking $TMUX to change footer/help hints and to show an escape-time hint or doctor check.
States Ctrl+B is tmux's default prefix and tmux catches it and never passes it to the pane program.
Explains escape-time wait, 500 ms before 3.5, and documents `set -sg escape-time 10` in tmux.conf.

Suggests checking $TMUX (and $ZELLIJ/$STY) to show working hints and to check escape-time with a notice.
The answer says Ctrl+B is tmux's default prefix and that tmux consumes it, so the app never receives it.
The answer explains that tmux holds a lone ESC for escape-time, gives the 500 ms default before 3.5, and suggests documenting `set -sg escape-time 10`.
The answer recommends a non-Ctrl/Alt binding such as `\` or a leader sequence, and notes that screen uses Ctrl+A.
The answer suggests showing the working binding in hints when `$TMUX` is set, and detecting tmux to check escape-time and show a hint.
